paragraphs: Rabbi Yochanan HaSandlar: Avot, chapter 4. In the Mishnah: Yevamot 12:5; Ketubbot 5:4; Kelim 5:5. He was Rabbi Meir’s and Rabbi Yehudah’s colleague: Chullin, chapter 1; Ketubbot, chapter 5, 58b; and Berakhot 22a and 30a. He was Rabbi Akiva’s student, transmitted in Rabbi Akiva’s name, and Rabbi Akiva ordained him in his youth. In the Jerusalem Talmud, beginning of Chomer BaKodesh, seven elders entered to intercalate the year in the Valley of Rimmon: Rabbi Meir, Rabbi Yehudah, Rabbi Yose, Rabbi Shimon, Rabbi Nechemyah, Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov, and Rabbi Yochanan HaSandlar. They asked: ‘How many higher standards apply to sacred food?’ Rabbi Meir said thirteen; Rabbi Yose said twelve. Rabbi Meir said: ‘Thus I heard from Rabbi Akiva: thirteen.’ Rabbi Yochanan HaSandlar told him: ‘I served Rabbi Akiva standing more than you served him sitting.’ They said: ‘Rabbi Yochanan HaSandlar is an Alexandrian’—meaning he was an Alexandrian—‘in truth’—meaning his service of Rabbi Akiva was a true matter. They rose with a kiss: that is, with such affection that they did not take offense at one another; see there. In the Jerusalem Talmud, the chapter Mitzvat Chalitzah, Rabbi Yochanan HaSandlar made himself look like a peddler and passed before the house where Rabbi Akiva was imprisoned. He proclaimed: ‘Who wants needles? If she performed chalitzah privately between him and her, what is the law?’ Rabbi Akiva looked out and said: ‘Do you have spindles? It is valid’ [a coded reply pairing Aramaic kushin with kasher]. He used to make sandals. Yuchasin, in the sequence of generations, writes that some say he drilled pearls, because the Targum renders raamot and gavish as sandalkhon. I saw in Benjamin’s Travels that he saw the vessel in which he used to soak the hides. In Sifrei, Rabbi Elazar be-Rabbi Shimon and Rabbi Yochanan HaSandlar questioned Rabbi Shimon. He and Rabbi Elazar ben Shammua set out for Rabbi Yehudah ben Beteira. Rabbi Yonatan ben Yosef; Rabbi Natan ben Avshalom. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel transmitted in his name. [I, the writer Yechiel, possess a written genealogical scroll stating that my maternal grandfather was of Rabbi Yochanan HaSandlar’s seed. The sequence of genealogy from him includes Rashi, light of the exile, the gaon Maharshal, and my aforementioned grandfather.] His burial is in the village of Meron; see Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai.
